title: Plegma
statementMd:
*This is a run-twice (communication) problem.*

There are two players: Player A and Player B. The jury will first interact with player A. After player A ends their interaction, the jury will interact with player B. Note that player A and player B may not directly pass information to each other; both players are only able to send information or receive information from the jury, but they may agree on the strategy they will use to communicate.

The jury has a **binary grid** $G$ of $n$ rows and $n$ columns (each cell of this grid has value either $0$ or $1$). Row $1$ is the top-most row, and column $1$ is the left-most column. The **connectivity** of this grid is defined as $1$ if there is a path going left, right, up, or down going through only cells with value $1$ connecting each pair of cells $(i_1,j_1)$ and $(i_2,j_2)$ with $G_{i_1,j_1}=G_{i_2,j_2}=1$. Note that moving diagonally is not allowed. It is guaranteed that there exists at least one cell with value of $1$ in this grid.

The jury first interacts with player A. The jury will give player A the grid $G$. After inspecting the grid, player A must determine **two integers** $r$ and $c$ and send them to the jury. At the start of player B's interaction, player B will receive **the values of all cells in the $r$'th row and all cells in the $c$'th column** from the jury. Note that player B is not given the values of $r$ and $c$.

Player A wants to ensure player B can determine the connectivity of $G$. Your task is to act as both players and find a strategy so that player B is able to determine the connectivity correctly. Note that the communicator of this task is not adaptive – that is, the grid given to you on the first run will be the same as the grid used to evaluate the connectivity.

## Input

Your code will be ran exactly two times on each test. On the first run, you will be Player A, and on the second Player B.

**First Run Input**

The first line of the input contains the string `first`. The purpose of this is so your program recognizes that this is its first run, and it should act as Player A.

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^4$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers $n$ and $C$ ($2 \leq n \leq 1000, 0 \leq C \leq 1$) – the size of the grid and the connectivity respectively.

The following $n$ lines contain information about the grid. The $i$th of these lines contains a binary string $G_i$ of length $n$, indicating the $i$-th row of the grid.

It is guaranteed that:

- The sum of $n^2$ does not exceed $2\cdot 10^6$ over all test cases
- The value of $C$ matches with the information in the grid – that is, if $C=1$, then the grid has connectivity $1$, and if $C=0$, then the grid has connectivity $0$.
- Each grid has at least one $1$ in the input.

**Second Run Input**

The first line of the input contains the string `second`. The purpose of this is so your program recognizes that this is its second run, and it should act as Player B.

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^4$). The description of the test cases follows. Note that this number is equal to $t$ from the first run input.

The first line of each test case contains exactly one integer $n$ — the size of the grid given on the $i$'th test case of the first run input.

The second line of each test case contains a binary string $G_{r, 1}G_{r, 2}\ldots G_{r, n}$ — the contents in row $r$ of the grid. Note that the integer $r$ is sent by player A to the jury at the end of their interaction of the $i$'th test case

The third line of each test case contains a binary string $G_{1, c}G_{2, c}\ldots G_{n, c}$ — the contents in column $c$ of the grid. Note that the integer $c$ is sent by player A to the jury at the end of their interaction of the $i$'th test case.

**Hacks**

To make hacks, use the following format:

The first line should contain exactly one integer $t$ $(1 \le t \le 10^4)$ — the number of grids. Then, $t$ blocks of input should follow.

The first line of each block of input must contain a single integer $n$ $(2 \le n \le 1000)$ — the size of the grid the jury will choose.

Each of the next $n$ lines should contain a binary string of size $n$. The $i$'th of these lines should contain $G_{i, 1}G_{i, 2}\ldots G_{i, n}$ — the contents of the $i$'th row of the grid the jury will choose.

There must exist at least a single cell with value of $1$ in each grid, and the sum of $n^2$ over all test cases should not exceed $2\cdot 10^6$.

Note that the connectivity of each grid is determined by the jury, and you do not need to output it for a hack.

## Output

For the first run, for each test case, output two integers $r$ and $c$ ($1 \leq r,c \leq n$). This indicates that you want the second run to receive the $r$-th row and the $c$-th column of the grid.

For the second run, for each test case, output an integer $C$ ($0 \leq C \leq 1$) – the connectivity of the grid.

## Note

On the first input example, the first grid is the following:

1110

On the first run, we know that $n = 2$. After inspecting the example, we can determine that the connectivity is $1$.

For the sake of this example, suppose Player A and Player B have agreed to some strategy where if the connectivity is $1$, then player A should send a row and a column that both end with $0$. In this case, row $2$ and column $2$ satisfies this strategy. **Note that this is an example strategy for the sake of demonstration, and using this strategy will not work for all cases.**

Then, take a look at the second run. Now, we are Player B. We receive that $n = 2$ and that the chosen row has values $r = [1, 0]$ and the chosen column has values $c = [1, 0]$. Since the last number of each row is $0$, player B uses the agreed upon strategy to determine that the connectivity is $1$.
statementZhMd:
*这是一道需要运行两次的（通信）题目。*

有两名玩家：玩家 A 和玩家 B。评测程序将首先与玩家 A 交互；在玩家 A 结束交互后，评测程序将与玩家 B 交互。注意，玩家 A 和玩家 B 不能直接互相传递信息；两名玩家都只能向评测程序发送信息或从评测程序接收信息，但他们可以事先约定将要使用的通信策略。

评测程序有一个 $n$ 行 $n$ 列的**二进制网格** $G$（网格的每个单元格的值要么是 $0$，要么是 $1$）。第 $1$ 行是最上面的一行，第 $1$ 列是最左边的一列。如果对于每一对满足 $G_{i_1,j_1}=G_{i_2,j_2}=1$ 的单元格 $(i_1,j_1)$ 和 $(i_2,j_2)$，都存在一条只经过值为 $1$ 的单元格、向左、向右、向上或向下移动的路径将它们连通，则该网格的**连通性**定义为 $1$。注意，不允许斜向移动。保证网格中至少存在一个值为 $1$ 的单元格。

评测程序首先与玩家 A 交互。评测程序会把网格 $G$ 交给玩家 A。在查看网格之后，玩家 A 必须确定**两个整数** $r$ 和 $c$ 并将其发送给评测程序。在玩家 B 的交互开始时，玩家 B 将从评测程序那里收到**第 $r$ 行的所有单元格和第 $c$ 列的所有单元格的值**。注意，玩家 B 不会被告知 $r$ 和 $c$ 的值。

玩家 A 想要确保玩家 B 能够确定 $G$ 的连通性。你的任务是同时扮演这两名玩家，找到一种策略，使得玩家 B 能够正确地确定连通性。注意，本题的通信程序不是自适应的——也就是说，第一次运行时给你的网格与用于评测连通性的网格是同一个。

## 输入格式

你的代码会在每个测试点上恰好运行两次。第一次运行时，你是玩家 A；第二次运行时，你是玩家 B。

**第一次运行的输入**

输入的第一行包含字符串 `first`。它的作用是让你的程序识别出这是第一次运行，从而扮演玩家 A。

每个测试包含多组测试用例。第一行包含测试用例的数量 $t$（$1 \le t \le 10^4$）。接下来是各组测试用例的描述。

每组测试用例的第一行包含两个整数 $n$ 和 $C$（$2 \leq n \leq 1000, 0 \leq C \leq 1$）——分别表示网格的大小和连通性。

接下来的 $n$ 行描述网格的信息。其中第 $i$ 行包含一个长度为 $n$ 的二进制字符串 $G_i$，表示网格的第 $i$ 行。

保证：

- 所有测试用例的 $n^2$ 之和不超过 $2\cdot 10^6$；
- $C$ 的值与网格中的信息一致——也就是说，若 $C=1$，则网格的连通性为 $1$；若 $C=0$，则网格的连通性为 $0$；
- 输入中的每个网格都至少含有一个 $1$。

**第二次运行的输入**

输入的第一行包含字符串 `second`。它的作用是让你的程序识别出这是第二次运行，从而扮演玩家 B。

每个测试包含多组测试用例。第一行包含测试用例的数量 $t$（$1 \le t \le 10^4$）。接下来是各组测试用例的描述。注意，这个数量与第一次运行输入中的 $t$ 相同。

每组测试用例的第一行恰好包含一个整数 $n$——即第一次运行输入中第 $i$ 组测试用例给出的网格的大小。

每组测试用例的第二行包含一个二进制字符串 $G_{r, 1}G_{r, 2}\ldots G_{r, n}$——网格第 $r$ 行的内容。注意，整数 $r$ 是玩家 A 在第 $i$ 组测试用例的交互结束时发送给评测程序的。

每组测试用例的第三行包含一个二进制字符串 $G_{1, c}G_{2, c}\ldots G_{n, c}$——网格第 $c$ 列的内容。注意，整数 $c$ 是玩家 A 在第 $i$ 组测试用例的交互结束时发送给评测程序的。

**Hack**

要进行 hack，请使用以下格式：

第一行应当恰好包含一个整数 $t$ $(1 \le t \le 10^4)$——网格的数量。随后是 $t$ 组输入。

每组输入的第一行必须包含一个整数 $n$ $(2 \le n \le 1000)$——评测程序将会选择的网格的大小。

接下来的 $n$ 行每行应当包含一个长度为 $n$ 的二进制字符串。其中第 $i$ 行应当包含 $G_{i, 1}G_{i, 2}\ldots G_{i, n}$——评测程序将会选择的网格第 $i$ 行的内容。

每个网格中必须至少存在一个值为 $1$ 的单元格，并且所有测试用例的 $n^2$ 之和不应超过 $2\cdot 10^6$。

注意，每个网格的连通性由评测程序决定，你在 hack 时无需输出它。

## 输出格式

第一次运行时，对于每组测试用例，输出两个整数 $r$ 和 $c$（$1 \leq r,c \leq n$）。这表示你希望第二次运行收到网格的第 $r$ 行和第 $c$ 列。

第二次运行时，对于每组测试用例，输出一个整数 $C$（$0 \leq C \leq 1$）——网格的连通性。

## 说明

在第一个输入样例中，第一个网格如下：

1110

在第一次运行中，我们知道 $n = 2$。检查这个样例后，我们可以确定连通性为 $1$。

为了便于说明这个例子，假设玩家 A 和玩家 B 已经约定了某种策略：如果连通性为 $1$，那么玩家 A 应当发送一行和一列，且这两者都以 $0$ 结尾。在本例中，第 $2$ 行和第 $2$ 列满足这一策略。**注意，这只是用于演示的示例策略，使用该策略并不能应对所有情况。**

然后，我们来看第二次运行。现在我们是玩家 B。我们得知 $n = 2$，并且所选行的值为 $r = [1, 0]$，所选列的值为 $c = [1, 0]$。由于行与列的最后一个数都是 $0$，玩家 B 按照约定的策略确定连通性为 $1$。
